problem: The flow chart is titled 'Knuckle joint sizing', but it includes a block 'Cotter — shear check' between 'Eye and fork' and 'Joint sized'. A knuckle joint has no cotter; its parts are eye, fork, pin and pin retainer. A student reading the chart will think a cotter is part of the knuckle joint.
fix: Remove the cotter node from the knuckle flow (Tension load → Rod diameter → Pin diameter → Eye and fork bearing check → Joint sized), or split the figure into two flows: one for the knuckle joint and a separate one for the cotter joint (cotter shear and bearing → spigot/socket/collar checks).

problem: The moment is never written, so the student cannot compute it. The sentence only says 'P at the centre and P/2 at each tine; then σb = M/Z'. The lever arm (half eye thickness plus half tine thickness) is missing.
fix: Add the moment: M = (P/2)(te/2 + tf/2) = P(te + tf)/4, with te the eye thickness and tf one tine thickness in mm, then σ<sub>bending</sub> = M/Z with Z = πdp³/32.

problem: The symbol σb is used twice with two different meanings: for bearing stress (σb = P/(dpte)) and for pin bending stress (σb = M/Z). In one section the same symbol names two different stresses.
fix: Use σ<sub>c</sub> or σ<sub>br</sub> for bearing (crushing) stress and σ<sub>b</sub> for bending stress, and state which is which the first time each appears.

problem: A<sub>net</sub> is described only in words ('the socket wall area left on both sides of the cotter slot'), so a student cannot put numbers into the check that the exam asks for.
fix: Give the expression: A<sub>net</sub> = (π/4)(D² − ds²) − (D − ds)t, where D is the socket outside diameter in mm, ds the spigot diameter in mm and t the cotter thickness in mm.
